doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Thanks, Giacomo Gates and goodbyes
summary: Mondello thanks the archive, praises Giacomo Gates and Glenn Zottola, and the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I’ve really enjoyed our conversation.
Oh this has been wonderful. Absolutely wonderful. I can’t thank you enough of course, and both Giacomo Gates, my dear friend, the “Genuine One.”

He really digs that that I call him that. But don’t tell him this, I mean he truly is a genuine artist, but I actually picked that up, I stole it from a can of Budweiser, because I saw the word “genuine” and I says you know what? That’s Gates. You know Gates carries the torch you know of, you know all of the Eddie Jefferson going all the way back to Pops.
Yep. He’s part of that Venn diagram.

Without a doubt. Thank Glenn Zottola as well, my savant friend. Thank you, Hamilton College, Milton Fillius, and the endowment, your jazz archive and Hamilton College’s jazz archive is something that, as we said before, that both young students and not-so- young students certainly would benefit tremendously. You know? I think that people — we live in an audio-visual world now, so people, you know TikTok and you know Twitter and all of that stuff, you know having people observe those videos. And you know I mean you’ve done over 400 of them, right?

So I mean that’s a monstrous buffet you know? So you know you do a few at a time or one at a time and things that are picked up and it’s a wonderful, wonderful, wonderful resource. And I certainly can’t thank you enough.
Well I’m glad you’re part of it now.
Thank you so very, very much.
All right. I’ll pause us here and we’ll say our good-byes.
